public_rationale: CNBC's report on its Technology Executive Council survey, run October 8 to 21, 2024, says 79% of respondents said their company was using Microsoft Copilot. It also says Copilot was introduced roughly one year earlier. Marcus wrote 'had tried,' which is close to 'using.' The same survey found that virtually no firms were on the fence about AI adoption, and that 63% said AI investment was accelerating. Among the surveyed tech leaders, AI was clearly not being ignored. The claim is supported for that population. The survey does not speak to the wider public.
limitations: Small, non-representative sample of tech executives at large firms.
'Using' at the company level is not the same as each respondent having tried it.
The 'refutation' holds only for the surveyed group.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The 79% Copilot trial rate among surveyed executives refutes the narrative that people are ignoring AI.
conditions: based on CNBC Technology Executive Council survey

our_interpretation: The checkable core is whether the October 2024 CNBC survey reported that about 79% of respondents had tried or were using Copilot, and whether that population was not ignoring AI.
'Refutation' is read as applying to the surveyed population (tech leaders at large firms). It is not read as a claim about the whole public.
'How new the product is' is read as Copilot having launched about a year earlier.
criteria.support_condition: The CNBC survey reports about 79% of respondents using Copilot, about a year after launch, and shows broad AI uptake among respondents.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The survey reports a materially different figure, or shows respondents largely not using or ignoring AI.
